library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ismaeil_2026_cariprazine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ismaeil_2026_cariprazine"))$description`
* Article: [J Clin Pharmacol 2026;66(7):e70243](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70243) (open access)
* Supplement: Supporting Information (Table S1 and Figures S1-S7)

Ismaeil 2026 adapts the adult cariprazine population PK model of Periclou
2021 (packaged as `Periclou_2021_cariprazine`) to children and adolescents. The
structure is unchanged, and every structural, race, sex and first-dose
parameter is fixed to its adult value. Only three things were re-estimated on
the pediatric data:

* the body-weight exponents on `CL/F` and `Vc/F` of cariprazine, DCAR and DDCAR,
  still referenced to the adult 79 kg (Equation 1);
* the between-subject variances on cariprazine `CL/F`, `Vc/F` and `Ka`, and on
  `CL/F` and `Vc/F` of each metabolite;
* the proportional residual errors for "full profile studies".

The three analytes were fitted one after the other with the preceding
analyte's parameters fixed, and they share one ODE system in the packaged file.

# Population

The analysis pooled two phase 1 studies (Table 2): 101 patients, of whom 25 were
children aged 10-12 years, 60 adolescents aged 13-17 years and 16 adults aged
18-40 years. Mean age was 16 years and mean body weight 59.6 kg (range
26.9-95.4 kg; 9 patients under 40 kg); 60% were male and 58% White, 41% Black
and 1% Asian. Study 1 enrolled adolescents with schizophrenia and children and
adolescents with bipolar I disorder (1.5, 3 or 4.5 mg once daily after
titration, 42 days); Study 2 enrolled adolescents and adults with schizophrenia
(1.5, 3 or 6 mg once daily, 28 days). The data hold 4237 concentrations
(cariprazine 1570, DCAR 1269, DDCAR 1398).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Ismaeil_2026_cariprazine")()$population`.

# Model structure

* `depot` receives each dose as a **zero-order input** over `DUR` = 2.57 h and
  empties into `central` at `Ka`.
* Cariprazine distributes to `peripheral1` (`Q3/F`) and `peripheral2`
  (`Q4/F`). Its elimination forms DCAR in `central_dcar`, which exchanges with
  `peripheral1_dcar`.
* DCAR elimination passes through one delay compartment, `transit1`
  (`DDKTR` = 0.0269 1/h), into `central_ddcar`, which exchanges with
  `peripheral1_ddcar`.
* A first-dose shift raises cariprazine `Vc/F`, `Vp1/F` and `Q3/F` and DCAR
  `Vc/F` and `Vp/F` until the second dose; the model builds it from
  `dosenum()`.
* Weight enters every `CL/F` and `Vc/F` as `(WT / 79)^theta`.

Dose records must use `rate = -2` so that rxode2 applies `dur(depot)`. Every
observation row returns all three concentrations; the event tables below place
observations on the ODE state `central` with `dvid = 1`.

The covariate `STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE` selects the residual error: 1 for
the full-profile studies the model was fitted to (both pediatric studies), 0 for
the sparse-sampling studies whose error is held at the adult value. All
simulations below set it to 1.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Ismaeil_2026_cariprazine")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode2(mod), which = "omega")
mod_adult <- readModelDb("Periclou_2021_cariprazine")

# ng/mL per nM (molecular weights 427.4, 413.4 and 399.7 g/mol for
# cariprazine, DCAR and DDCAR), as in the Periclou 2021 article.
mw <- c(CAR = 0.4274, DCAR = 0.4134, DDCAR = 0.3997)

make_events <- function(id, dose_times, amts, obs_times, covs) {
  ev <- rbind(
    data.frame(id = id, time = dose_times, amt = amts, rate = -2, evid = 1L,
               cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
               evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  )
  ev <- ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
  cbind(ev, covs[rep(1, nrow(ev)), , drop = FALSE], row.names = NULL)
}

to_nM <- function(sim) {
  if (!"id" %in% names(sim)) sim$id <- 1L
  sim |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      CAR = Cc / mw[["CAR"]],
      DCAR = Cc_dcar / mw[["DCAR"]],
      DDCAR = Cc_ddcar / mw[["DDCAR"]],
      Total = CAR + DCAR + DDCAR
    )
}

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

white_male <- function(WT) {
  data.frame(WT = WT, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, RACE_JAPANESE = 0,
             STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE = 1)
}
```

# Deterministic checks

## Weight exponents: steady-state AUC equals Dose / CL

Every molecule of cariprazine eliminated becomes DCAR and every molecule of
DCAR becomes DDCAR, so at steady state each analyte's AUC over one dosing
interval must equal `Dose / CL` of that analyte. Checking this at 35 kg, far
from the 79 kg reference, confirms that each re-estimated weight exponent sits
on the right clearance.

```{r mass-balance}
wt_chk <- 35
ev_mb <- make_events(1L, seq(0, 139 * 24, by = 24), 4.5,
                     seq(139 * 24, 140 * 24, by = 0.05), white_male(wt_chk))
mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_mb, returnType = "data.frame")
cl_expected <- c(21.5 * (wt_chk / 79)^0.0977, 77.3 * (wt_chk / 79)^0.0697,
                 9.24 * (wt_chk / 79)^0.511)
mb_tab <- data.frame(
  analyte = c("CAR", "DCAR", "DDCAR"),
  auc_tau = c(trap(mb$time, mb$Cc), trap(mb$time, mb$Cc_dcar), trap(mb$time, mb$Cc_ddcar)),
  dose_over_cl = 4500 / cl_expected
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_tau - dose_over_cl) / dose_over_cl)
mb_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Analyte" = analyte, "AUC over 24 h (ng*h/mL)" = auc_tau,
                "Dose / CL (ng*h/mL)" = dose_over_cl, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical 35 kg White male, 4.5 mg once daily, day 140.")
# Same parameters on both sides, so only numerical error separates them.
stopifnot(max(abs(mb_tab$pct_diff)) < 0.5)
```

## Pediatric versus adult weight effects

At the 79 kg reference the pediatric and adult models share every typical
value. Away from it they differ only through the weight exponents; the
pediatric model's shallower exponents on `Vc/F` (cariprazine 0.998 vs 1.66, DCAR
0.284 vs 1.18) and on DDCAR `Vc/F` (0.244 vs 0.881) change the within-interval
shape, while the DDCAR clearance exponent (0.511 vs 0.427) sets most of the
total exposure.

```{r typical-profiles, fig.height = 4}
obs_ss <- seq(41 * 24, 42 * 24, by = 0.25)
typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(35, 55, 79), function(w) {
  ev <- make_events(1L, seq(0, 41 * 24, by = 24), 4.5, obs_ss, white_male(w))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |> to_nM() |>
      dplyr::mutate(model = "Ismaeil 2026 (pediatric)"),
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode2(mod_adult)), ev,
                    returnType = "data.frame") |> to_nM() |>
      dplyr::mutate(model = "Periclou 2021 (adult)")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = paste(w, "kg"))
}))
ggplot(typ, aes(time / 24 - 41, Total, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~WT) +
  labs(x = "Time after the 42nd daily 4.5 mg dose (days)", y = "Total CAR (nM)",
       colour = NULL, title = "Typical White male, total cariprazine at steady state")

# At 79 kg the two models must coincide exactly.
at79 <- typ |> dplyr::filter(WT == "79 kg") |>
  dplyr::select(model, time, Total) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = Total)
stopifnot(max(abs(at79[[2]] - at79[[3]]) / at79[[3]]) < 1e-6)
```

# Virtual cohorts (Table 1, Table S1)

The paper drew 1000 children aged 10-12 years and 1000 adolescents aged
13-17 years, sampled body weight from the CDC weight-for-age charts, split the
children at 40 kg, and gave every virtual patient the sex and race
proportions of the adult population (33.6% female; 45.6% White, 34.9% Black,
14.3% Asian, 1.7% Japanese, 3.5% other). The CDC tables are not distributed
with this package, so weight is drawn here from a log-normal distribution:

* children: median 38.3 kg and log-scale SD 0.24, which puts 57.1% of children
  under 40 kg -- the 571 of 1000 in Table S1 -- and is then split into the
  Table S1 ranges 23.1-40.0 kg and 40.0-93.6 kg;
* adolescents: median 55 kg (close to the sex-averaged CDC median at
  15 years) with the same spread, kept inside the Table S1 range
  31.7-157 kg;
* adults (legacy adult model): normal with the Periclou 2021 mean and SD
  (78.9 +/- 18.7 kg) inside its observed range 33.1-155.1 kg.

Each group has 200 virtual patients, re-used for every dose level.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260313)
n_sub <- 200

draw_in_range <- function(n, rdraw, lo, hi) {
  w <- numeric(0)
  while (length(w) < n) {
    x <- rdraw(4 * n)
    w <- c(w, x[x >= lo & x < hi])
  }
  w[seq_len(n)]
}
rlnorm_med <- function(med) function(n) med * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.24))

make_cohort <- function(group, wt) {
  race <- sample(c("White", "Black", "Asian", "Japanese", "Other"), n_sub, replace = TRUE,
                 prob = c(45.6, 34.9, 14.3, 1.7, 3.5))
  data.frame(group = group, WT = wt, SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.336),
             RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "Black"),
             RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "Asian"),
             RACE_JAPANESE = as.integer(race == "Japanese"),
             STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE = 1)
}

cohorts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort("Children (<40 kg)", draw_in_range(n_sub, rlnorm_med(38.3), 23.1, 40)),
  make_cohort("Children (>=40 kg)", draw_in_range(n_sub, rlnorm_med(38.3), 40, 93.6)),
  make_cohort("Adolescents", draw_in_range(n_sub, rlnorm_med(55), 31.7, 157)),
  make_cohort("Adults", draw_in_range(n_sub, function(n) rnorm(n, 78.9, 18.7), 33.1, 155.1))
)
cohorts |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), median_wt = median(WT), min_wt = min(WT),
                   max_wt = max(WT), pct_female = 100 * mean(SEXF)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "N" = n, "Median weight (kg)" = median_wt,
                "Min (kg)" = min_wt, "Max (kg)" = max_wt, "Female (%)" = pct_female) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohorts.")
```

# Steady-state exposure after 42 days (replicates Figure 2 and Table S1)

Each group receives a fixed daily dose for 42 days (Table 1): 1.5, 3 or 4.5 mg
in the pediatric groups with the pediatric model, and 1.5, 3, 4.5 or 6 mg in
the adults with the legacy adult model. Total CAR is the molar sum of the
three analytes, and exposure is taken over the 42nd dosing interval. Residual
error is not part of these exposure metrics; the solved `Cc` columns are
individual predictions.

```{r ss-simulate}
doses <- list(
  "Children (<40 kg)" = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), "Children (>=40 kg)" = c(1.5, 3, 4.5),
  "Adolescents" = c(1.5, 3, 4.5), "Adults" = c(1.5, 3, 4.5, 6)
)
obs_grid <- seq(41 * 24, 42 * 24, by = 1)
arm_id <- 0L
ss_events <- list()
for (g in names(doses)) {
  coh <- cohorts[cohorts$group == g, ]
  for (d in doses[[g]]) {
    arm_id <- arm_id + 1L
    ss_events[[arm_id]] <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
      make_events((arm_id - 1L) * n_sub + i, seq(0, 41 * 24, by = 24), d, obs_grid,
                  coh[i, -1])
    })) |>
      dplyr::mutate(group = g, treatment = paste(d, "mg"))
  }
}
ss_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(ss_events)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ss_events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))

ev_ped <- ss_events |> dplyr::filter(group != "Adults")
ev_adu <- ss_events |> dplyr::filter(group == "Adults")
ss_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_ped, keep = c("group", "treatment"), returnType = "data.frame"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult, dplyr::select(ev_adu, -STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE),
                  keep = c("group", "treatment"), returnType = "data.frame")
) |>
  to_nM() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, group, treatment, Total)
```

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- ss_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Total)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = time - 41 * 24)
nca_dose <- ss_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 41 * 24) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, group, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Total ~ time | group + treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | group + treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 6}
table_s1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~treatment, ~auclast, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "Children (<40 kg)", "1.5 mg", 700, 32.0, 27.2,
  "Children (<40 kg)", "3 mg", 1394, 63.5, 53.7,
  "Children (<40 kg)", "4.5 mg", 2083, 95.8, 80.9,
  "Children (>=40 kg)", "1.5 mg", 619, 28.6, 23.8,
  "Children (>=40 kg)", "3 mg", 1230, 56.6, 47.3,
  "Children (>=40 kg)", "4.5 mg", 1846, 84.5, 72.1,
  "Adolescents", "1.5 mg", 570, 26.4, 22.1,
  "Adolescents", "3 mg", 1163, 53.6, 45.0,
  "Adolescents", "4.5 mg", 1715, 78.8, 65.9,
  "Adults", "1.5 mg", 538, 25.0, 20.9,
  "Adults", "3 mg", 1045, 48.7, 40.5,
  "Adults", "4.5 mg", 1578, 72.6, 60.9,
  "Adults", "6 mg", 2091, 96.5, 81.1
)
grp_levels <- c("Adults", "Adolescents", "Children (<40 kg)", "Children (>=40 kg)")
nca_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, grp_levels))
ggplot(nca_ind, aes(treatment, PPORRES, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = table_s1 |>
               tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auclast, cmax, cmin), names_to = "PPTESTCD",
                                   values_to = "PPORRES") |>
               dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, grp_levels)),
             aes(group = group), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
             shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~PPTESTCD, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(auclast = "AUCtau,ss (nM*h)", cmax = "Cmax,ss (nM)",
                                      cmin = "Ctrough,ss (nM)"))) +
  labs(x = "Daily dose", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Steady-state total CAR after 42 days of fixed dosing",
       caption = "Boxes: simulated. Crosses: Table S1 medians of Ismaeil 2026. Replicates Figure 2.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Comparison against Table S1

```{r nca-compare}
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = table_s1,
  by = c("group", "treatment"),
  units = c(auclast = "nM*h", cmax = "nM", cmin = "nM"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Table S1 median steady-state total CAR exposure. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-gate}
sim_med <- nca_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(group = as.character(group)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    table_s1 |> tidyr::pivot_longer(c(auclast, cmax, cmin), names_to = "PPTESTCD",
                                    values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("group", "treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
ped <- sim_med$group != "Adults"
# Centre and envelope of the 39 per-arm medians. At authoring the pediatric
# medians sat 2-18% above Table S1 (median about 11%) and the adult (Periclou
# 2021) medians 7-15% above, so the offset comes from the shared adult
# structure (see Assumptions and deviations). A mis-transcribed weight
# exponent, clearance or dose moves whole groups by far more than this.
stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_med) == 39,
  abs(median(sim_med$pct_diff[ped])) < 20,
  quantile(abs(sim_med$pct_diff[ped]), 0.9) < 30,
  abs(median(sim_med$pct_diff[!ped])) < 25
)

# The quantity behind the dosing recommendation: exposure relative to adults
# at the same dose. Children under 40 kg have the highest exposure (about 20%
# above the next group, so the ordering is robust); the gaps between
# children >= 40 kg, adolescents and adults are smaller than the cohort noise of
# a 200-subject median, so those are compared as ratios, not as an ordering.
auc45 <- sim_med |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast", treatment == "4.5 mg") |>
  dplyr::select(group, sim, ref) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sim_ratio = sim / sim[group == "Adults"],
                ref_ratio = ref / ref[group == "Adults"])
stopifnot(
  auc45$sim[auc45$group == "Children (<40 kg)"] == max(auc45$sim),
  all(abs(auc45$sim_ratio - auc45$ref_ratio) < 0.2)
)
auc45 |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "Simulated AUC (nM*h)" = sim, "Table S1 AUC (nM*h)" = ref,
                "Simulated ratio to adults" = sim_ratio, "Table S1 ratio to adults" = ref_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "4.5 mg once daily: median total CAR AUCtau,ss relative to adults.")
```

# Titration (replicates Figure 3)

Figure 3 titrates the pediatric groups with 0.5 mg on days 1-2, 1.5 mg on
days 3-4, 3 mg on days 5-7 and 4.5 mg from day 8, and the adults with 1.5 mg on
day 1, 3 mg on days 2-4, 4.5 mg on days 5-7 and 6 mg from day 8 (the dose labels
printed in the Figure 3 insets), for 42 days.

```{r titration, fig.height = 6}
amts_ped <- c(0.5, 0.5, 1.5, 1.5, 3, 3, 3, rep(4.5, 35))
amts_adu <- c(1.5, 3, 3, 3, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, rep(6, 35))
# Troughs are sampled 0.01 h before each dose: a sample at the dose time
# itself already sees the post-first-dose volumes.
trough_times <- 1:41 * 24 - 0.01
obs_tit <- sort(c(seq(0, 42 * 24, by = 2), trough_times))
tit_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(grp_levels), function(k) {
  g <- grp_levels[k]
  coh <- cohorts[cohorts$group == g, ]
  amts <- if (g == "Adults") amts_adu else amts_ped
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
    make_events((k - 1L) * n_sub + i, seq(0, 41 * 24, by = 24), amts, obs_tit, coh[i, -1])
  })) |>
    dplyr::mutate(group = g)
}))
tit_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, dplyr::filter(tit_events, group != "Adults"), keep = "group",
                  returnType = "data.frame"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult,
                  dplyr::filter(tit_events, group == "Adults") |>
                    dplyr::select(-STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE),
                  keep = "group", returnType = "data.frame")
) |>
  to_nM()
tit_sum <- tit_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q05 = quantile(Total, 0.05), Q50 = median(Total),
                   Q95 = quantile(Total, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ped_panels <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(grp_levels[-1], function(g) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tit_sum |> dplyr::filter(group == g) |> dplyr::mutate(series = g),
    tit_sum |> dplyr::filter(group == "Adults") |> dplyr::mutate(series = "Adults (6 mg)")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(panel = g)
}))
ggplot(ped_panels, aes(time / 24, Q50, colour = series, fill = series)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Total CAR (nM)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Total CAR during titration (median, 5th-95th percentile)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Ismaeil 2026.")
```

```{r titration-check}
# During titration (days 1-7) the lower pediatric doses keep the median total
# CAR below the adult median at every daily trough, as the paper reports.
trough_days <- tit_sum |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% trough_times[1:7]) |>
  dplyr::select(group, time, Q50) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = Q50)
stopifnot(
  all(trough_days[["Adolescents"]] < trough_days[["Adults"]]),
  all(trough_days[["Children (<40 kg)"]] < trough_days[["Adults"]]),
  all(trough_days[["Children (>=40 kg)"]] < trough_days[["Adults"]])
)
trough_days |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = round(time / 24)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Day" = time) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median total CAR (nM) at the end of each titration day.")
```

# Simulated concentrations with residual error

A short check that the full-profile residual error is active: concentrations
of 200 adolescents at 4.5 mg on day 42, with the individual prediction (`Cc`)
and the simulated observation (`sim`) for cariprazine.

```{r residual}
ev_res <- ss_events |> dplyr::filter(group == "Adolescents", treatment == "4.5 mg")
res_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_res, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(CMT == 10)
rel_err <- log(res_sim$sim / res_sim$Cc)
# A proportional SD of 0.107 gives a log-ratio SD close to 0.107.
stopifnot(abs(sd(rel_err[is.finite(rel_err)]) - 0.107) < 0.02)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual errors are read as standard deviations.** Tables 3-5 print the
  proportional errors without a scale. They sit in the parameter table with
  %RSE and confidence intervals, as error terms coded on a `THETA` usually do,
  while the IIV is printed as variances alongside a %CV column. The width of
  the printed confidence intervals also fits an SD better: relative to the
  estimate they are 1.3-1.6 times the minimum width an SD estimated from 1270-
  1570 observations can have, whereas a variance would need intervals 0.65-0.8
  times its minimum width. The values are therefore encoded as SDs.
- **Which studies are "full profile studies".** The re-estimated residual
  errors apply to "full profile studies"; the fixed values are the adult
  model's errors for the other studies (Periclou 2021 estimated residual
  variability separately for phase 1 and phase 2/3 studies but did not print
  it). Both pediatric studies are full-profile studies, so every observation of
  the model-development data carries `STUDY_CARIPRAZINE_FULLPROFILE = 1`.
- **Table 5 'Proportional error DCAR (fixed)'** is listed in the DDCAR table,
  next to the DDCAR full-profile error; it is taken as the fixed DDCAR error of
  the other studies.
- **DDCAR age effect.** Table 5 lists a power of DDCAR `Vc/F` on age fixed to
  0, with no reference age. It has no effect and is not encoded; age is
  recorded under `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Units printed in Table 3.** `Q3/F` is printed in L and `DUR` as "DUR/F, h";
  they are a clearance in L/h and a duration in h, as in Periclou 2021.
- **Model structure from Periclou 2021.** Ismaeil 2026 describes the structure
  in prose and fixes every structural value to the adult model; the equations
  (zero-order input into the depot, transit-delayed DDCAR formation, the
  first-dose indicator) follow Periclou 2021, as in `Periclou_2021_cariprazine`.
  The first-dose shift is built from `dosenum()` and switches off at the second
  dose; a sample drawn at the exact time of the second dose already sees the
  later-dose volumes, so the titration troughs are taken 0.01 h before each
  dose.
- **Mass chain.** Metabolite formation is amount for amount in mg of dose and
  the metabolite parameters are apparent, as in the adult model.
- **Steady-state exposure sits about 11% above Table S1.** The pediatric
  medians are 2-18% above Table S1. The adult legacy model shows the same
  offset under the same simulation, 7-15% above the adult rows of Table S1, and
  the `Periclou_2021_cariprazine` article finds that model 8-15% above
  Periclou 2021 Table 3. The offset is therefore shared with the adult
  structure (the metabolite molar conversion and the authors' use of the
  observed adult dataset are possible sources), and the pediatric-to-adult
  exposure ratios that drove the dosing decision agree within about 0.06.
  The simulated gap between children of at least 40 kg and adolescents is
  smaller than in Table S1 (ratios to adults 1.15 vs 1.13 here, 1.17 vs 1.09
  in Table S1).
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight is drawn from log-normal distributions anchored to
  the Table S1 split at 40 kg and weight ranges rather than from the CDC LMS
  tables the paper used; the adolescent median of 55 kg is an assumption. Sex
  and race follow the adult proportions, as in the paper. No correlation
  between weight, sex and race is imposed.
- **Adult titration.** Table 1 prints 1.5 mg on days 1-2 and 3 mg on days 3-4
  for adults, while the text and the Figure 3 insets give 1.5 mg on day 1 and
  3 mg from day 2; Figure 3 is replicated with the inset doses.
- **IIV.** Off-diagonal elements are not reported; the random effects are
  independent.
- **Errata.** No correction to this article is listed in Europe PMC as of
  2026-11-14.
